title: Si bien: aunque, a pesar de que

sections.content: Si bien (although, while it's true that) introduces a concession -- it grants a fact without letting that fact undercut the main point that follows. It's more formal than aunque and common in written and analytical Spanish. It's typically followed by the indicative when the concession is a stated fact.

items.spanish: Presidentes elegidos democráticamente que, si bien habían llegado al poder por las urnas, gobernaron después concentrando facultades excepcionales en sus propias manos.
items.english: Democratically elected presidents who, although they had come to power through the ballot box, then governed by concentrating exceptional powers in their own hands.

items.spanish: Si bien el líder había sido votado legítimamente, una vez en el cargo actuaba como si el pueblo le hubiera delegado el derecho a gobernar sin mayores controles.
items.english: Although the leader had been legitimately voted in, once in office he acted as though the people had delegated to him the right to govern without much oversight.

items.spanish: Si bien Carlos Salinas de Gortari impulsó una ambiciosa apertura económica que culminó con el TLCAN, su gobierno también fue acusado de concentrar un poder presidencial casi sin contrapesos.
items.english: Although Carlos Salinas de Gortari drove an ambitious economic opening that culminated in NAFTA, his government was also accused of concentrating presidential power with almost no checks.

items.spanish: Si bien cada caso tuvo su propio desenlace, el patrón regional quedó claro.
items.english: Although each case had its own outcome, the regional pattern was clear.

sections.content: Si bien can open a sentence or sit mid-sentence, always followed by a comma before the main clause. Don't confuse it with si (if) + bien (well) -- as a fixed phrase it means although, not "if well".
